advances: Actual four consecutive integer fibers with common simplex shape, restricted opposite endpoint order, and a sufficient near-equal-middle range. No all-order claim.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
A common invertible continuous affine change allows $T$ to be the standard simplex, with all masses changing by the same Jacobian. Write $g$ for its centroid, $K=T-g$, and first consider the common-vertex model. At base $1$ use the triple $aT,bT,T$. With $\zeta=z-1$, the shear $x'=x-bg-\zeta(1-b)g$ centers both the middle and the right endpoint, giving $bK$ and $K$. Its left endpoint lies inside $bK$: after adding $bg$ it is $aT+(1-b)g$, all coordinates nonnegative and coordinate sum at most $a+d(1-b)/(d+1)\le b$. Keep $bK$ on the right and the whole left endpoint as its subset. A nonvertical through-centroid cap has opposite real thresholds at the two endpoints. Apply 4b772ae7fa6b3293 on $bK$ to give the first payment.

At base $2$ use the triple $bT,T,cT$. With $\zeta=z-2$, use $x'=x-g-\zeta(1-b)g$ to center the left endpoint and the middle as $bK,K$. After adding $bg$ to the transformed right endpoint and to $bK$, the two bodies become $cT-2(1-b)g$ and $bT$. Their intersection has nonnegative coordinates and coordinate sum at most $c-2d(1-b)/(d+1)\le b$. Conversely these inequalities suffice for the intersection, so it is $hT$ when $h>0$, or is null or empty when $h=0$. Keep its inverse translate as the right subset (use the empty subset if $h=0$). Apply 4b772ae7fa6b3293 with the two copies of $bK$ on the middle and left, reversing the endpoint roles. The remaining middle shell contributes exactly $(1-b^d)$ times the through-centroid cap volume of $K$, which is at least $\Gamma(1-b^d)V$ by the empty-subset case of the same fact, choosing the endpoint threshold past the support. This gives the second payment. Discarded fiber mass is nonnegative. Pure-base through-caps at bases $1,2$ contain at least $(b^d+a^d)V$ and $(1+c^d)V$, respectively, which suffice since $\Gamma,\lambda\le1$ and $h\le c$. Every closed containing cap contains its parallel through-cap.

For translated fibers $m_z+r_z K$, fix one anchor $j=1$ or $2$ and one nonzero continuous normal $u$. Let $v$ be a minimizing vertex for $u$ on $K$ and $L=-u\cdot v>0$. Actual compatibility implies the anchored Minkowski inclusions at $j$. Apply 155691fc3768c06f at $-u/\lVert u\rVert$, multiply by $-\lVert u\rVert$, and get a slope $s$ such that $u\cdot(m_z-m_j)\ge L(r_z-r_j)+s(z-j)$. For $X\in K$, the original through-cap margin at $m_z+r_zX$ is therefore at least the margin with adjusted base tilt $\beta+s$ at the comparison point $r_jv+r_z(X-v)$. The two maps have identical volume Jacobian. A linear simplex vertex permutation $P$ of $K$ takes $-g$ to $v$ and has absolute determinant one. The affine map $x'\mapsto P^{-1}(x'-r_jv)$ sends the comparison fibers to $r_zT$ and the mark to $r_jg$, preserving the summed cap volumes. Thus the common-vertex through-cap payments hold in every original direction. Pure-base caps have identical masses under comparison.

The sharpness assertion of 4b772ae7fa6b3293 and the coefficient-$1/2$ inequality of 7ad3d72ee6061cf3 imply $\lambda\ge1/2>\Gamma$ for $d\ge2$, where the last strict inequality follows from $(1+1/d)^d>2$. Thus $t>1$. Subtracting $\Gamma M/2$ from the maximum of the two payments and dividing by $\Gamma V$ gives precisely the scalar certificate with $A=a^d$. Its weighted-gap bound, clipped loss and uniform sufficient condition give the remaining claims. For $d=2$, $\lambda=7/9$, $t=7/4$, $R=5/2$, and the right-hand threshold is $81/280$, equivalent to the stated cutoff.

statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $T$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$, and suppose the only positive-volume integer fibers of an actual convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ are translates of $aT,bT,T,cT$ at $0,1,2,3$, where $0<a\le2b-1$, $1/2<b\le1$, and $0<c\le b$. Write $y_1,y_2$ for the actual own-fiber centroids at bases $1,2$, and use raw mixed depth $D$ given by the infimum of sums of fiber volumes over all closed containing ambient halfspaces. Set $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$, $\lambda=[(2d/(d+1))^{d/(d-1)}-1]^{d-1}$, $t=\lambda/\Gamma$, $R=2t-1$, $p=d-1$, $x=2d(1-b)/(d+1)$, and $h=[c-x]_+$. Then
$$D(y_1)\ge V(\Gamma b^d+\lambda a^d),\qquad D(y_2)\ge V(\Gamma+\lambda h^d).$$
For $M=V(a^d+b^d+1+c^d)$ and $J=(1-R^{-1/p})^{-p}$,
$$\max\{D(y_1),D(y_2)\}\ge\Gamma M/2+\frac{\Gamma V}{2t}[(t-1)(1-b^d)-tJx^d].$$
The sharper clipped loss over $0\le v\le b$ in the scalar certificate can replace $Jx^d$. In particular one of these two centroids reaches normalized depth $\Gamma/2$ whenever
$$\frac{1-b}{b}\le(1-R^{-1/p})\left[\frac{d(t-1)}{t(2d/(d+1))^d}\right]^{1/p}.$$
For $d=2$ this last sufficient condition is $b\ge280/361$.
title: Sharp subset payments at both centroids of an opposite-order simplex peak
